# How to align a thematic layer to a local reference layer

This how-to explains how to use brdrQ when you have your own reference layer and want to align a thematic layer to it.

Use this page when you want a practical workflow. For the full parameter reference, see [Autocorrectborders](autocorrectborders.md).

## Goal

You have a thematic layer, for example project zones, management areas, inventories, or administrative boundaries. These geometries should follow a more authoritative local reference layer.

The goal is to create:

* a `RESULT_DIST_...` layer with the aligned geometries;
* `DIFF_DIST_...`, `DIFF_PLUS_DIST_...`, and `DIFF_MIN_DIST_...` layers to understand what changed;
* optionally a `CORRECTION_DIST_...` layer when you want to review uncertain features in QGIS.

## Use This When

Use this workflow when:

* your reference data is already available as a QGIS vector layer;
* both thematic and reference data are in the same projected CRS, with meters as unit;
* every thematic feature has a stable unique ID;
* you want to control the alignment against your own data instead of an on-the-fly web reference.

Do not use this workflow for updating an old GRB-based dataset to a newer GRB version. For that use case, start from [GRB Updater](autoupdateborders.md).

## Input You Need

Prepare two layers in QGIS:

| Layer | Required | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Thematic layer | Yes | The layer you want to align. Polygon input is the main use case, but line and point workflows are also possible. |
| Thematic ID field | Yes | Must be unique and stable. This makes output traceable. |
| Local reference layer | Yes | The layer that represents the geometry you want to align to. |
| Reference ID field | Yes | Must identify reference features. Use a stable field, not a temporary display label. |

Before running the tool, check:

* both layers have the same projected CRS;
* the local reference layer has a spatial index, especially for larger datasets;
* the thematic ID has no duplicates;
* the reference layer is stored locally when possible, not on a slow network or cloud-synced path.

## Recommended Settings

Start with a conservative setup and only make it more aggressive when the result is too limited.

| Parameter | Recommended start | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Reference` | `LOCREF` | Uses your local reference layer. |
| `Local reference layer` | your reference layer | The geometric target for the alignment. |
| `Reference ID` | unique reference field | Keeps reference features traceable. |
| `RELEVANT_DISTANCE` | `2` to `5` meters | Limits how far geometries may move. |
| `PREDICTIONS` | `NO_PREDICTIONS` for first scan | Fast first result. |
| `Prediction Strategy` | `BEST` when predictions are enabled | Gives one practical result per feature. |
| `Full Reference Strategy` | `PREFER_FULL_REFERENCE` | Prefers candidates that fully match reference coverage. |
| `REVIEW_PERCENTAGE` | `10` | Sends larger changes to review when a review layer is used. |
| `GENERATE_CORRECTION_LAYER` | `False` for direct output, `True` for review | Keeps the output aligned with your workflow. |

## Steps In QGIS

1. Load the thematic layer and the local reference layer in QGIS.
2. Open `Processing Toolbox` -> `brdrQ` -> `Autocorrectborders (BULK)`.
3. Set `Thematic Layer` to your thematic layer.
4. Set `Thematic ID` to the unique ID field of the thematic layer.
5. Set `Reference` to `LOCREF`.
6. Set `Local reference layer` and `Reference ID`.
7. Start with `RELEVANT_DISTANCE=2` or `5`, depending on the expected deviation.
8. Choose your output workflow:
   * direct output: set `GENERATE_CORRECTION_LAYER=False`;
   * review in QGIS: set `GENERATE_CORRECTION_LAYER=True`.
9. Run the algorithm.

## Expected Output

The primary output is:

* `RESULT_DIST_...`: the aligned geometries;
* `DIFF_DIST_...`: all differences between original and result;
* `DIFF_PLUS_DIST_...`: geometry added by the alignment;
* `DIFF_MIN_DIST_...`: geometry removed by the alignment.

If enabled, brdrQ also creates:

* `CORRECTION_DIST_...`: an optional review/workflow layer with `brdrq_state`.

You can use `RESULT_DIST_...` and the `DIFF_` layers directly. You do not need the `CORRECTION_` layer unless your workflow includes manual review in QGIS or FeatureAligner.

## How To Check The Result

Start with the difference layers:

* large `DIFF_PLUS_` or `DIFF_MIN_` areas can indicate too high a `RELEVANT_DISTANCE`;
* many tiny differences can be normal when the source data was drawn against a less precise reference;
* unexpected changes far from the reference may indicate a wrong CRS, wrong reference layer, or unsuitable distance.

Then inspect the result layer:

* check whether the result follows the intended reference boundaries;
* compare a few typical features and a few edge cases;
* verify that feature IDs are still traceable.

If you used the review workflow, inspect `brdrq_state` in the `CORRECTION_DIST_...` layer:

| `brdrq_state` | What to do |
| :--- | :--- |
| `not_changed` | Usually no action needed. |
| `auto_updated` | Check by sample or according to your QA rules. |
| `to_review` | Inspect in QGIS or FeatureAligner before accepting. |
| `to_update` | Handle manually or use FeatureAligner as a starting point. |

## When To Use Predictions

Use `PREDICTIONS=NO_PREDICTIONS` for a first fast scan. This gives a quick result at the configured `RELEVANT_DISTANCE`.

Switch to `PREDICTIONS=PREDICTIONS` when:

* the result is unstable or ambiguous;
* you want brdr evaluations such as `prediction_unique` or `to_check_prediction_multi`;
* you want to compare candidate distances before accepting an alignment.

Use `Prediction Strategy=ALL` only for analysis. In that mode, brdrQ does not create a `CORRECTION_` review layer because the output contains all candidate predictions instead of one selected result per feature.

## Common Pitfalls

| Problem | Likely cause | What to do |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Output is empty or wrong | CRS mismatch or non-projected CRS | Use the same projected CRS in meters for both layers. |
| Processing is slow | Large reference layer without spatial index | Create a spatial index or store the layer locally. |
| Too many large changes | `RELEVANT_DISTANCE` is too high | Lower the distance and rerun. |
| Too little alignment | `RELEVANT_DISTANCE` is too low | Increase gradually, for example from `2` to `5`. |
| Review layer not created | `GENERATE_CORRECTION_LAYER=False` or `Prediction Strategy=ALL` | Use direct output, or enable the review layer with a one-result strategy such as `BEST`. |
| Results are hard to trace | Non-unique thematic ID | Fix the ID field before running the tool. |
